dynamic_rules.description: Before any trade entry, verify if the market is in Balance (range day, P-shape or b-shape profile consolidation) or Imbalance (trend day, active value migration). Trade Mean Reversion (buy VAL, sell VAH) only during Balance; trade breakouts/continuation only during Imbalance. Skip trading if in a transition state with mixed delta and choppy horizontal overlap inside the Value Area.

Validate Initial Balance (IB) range breakouts only when a candle BODY (not just the wick) closes completely outside the IB High or IB Low. If only the wick extends beyond the boundary, treat it as a liquidity sweep and prepare for a contrarian Failed Auction setup. Do not chase breakout candle wicks without delta confirmation.

Do not enter reversal or contrarian trades on the first vertical spike (First Drive) to prevent being swept. Wait for a second test of the extreme level (Second Drive). Enter only if the Second Drive shows delta exhaustion, institutional absorption (effort vs no result), or a clear delta flip, confirming that the initial breakout has failed.

Never place stop losses at obvious wick extremes, support/resistance lines, or round numbers — primary targets for liquidity sweeps. Place stops structurally behind dense HVN clusters, POC lines, or large Big Trade walls (observable in M1 footprint). For SHORT: stop goes ABOVE the nearest counter-trend BUY cluster. For LONG: stop goes BELOW the nearest counter-trend SELL cluster. Add 1-2pt buffer beyond the wall.
Adjust contract size inversely to structural stop distance. Wider stop = smaller size to keep absolute dollar risk constant. Do not use fixed contract sizing across different volatility regimes.
Two-target scale-out: at Target 1 (nearest VP ledge, POC, or local HVN) exit 50% and trail remaining stop to Breakeven. Do not exit 100% at Target 1 on strong imbalance days.

Do not trade AGAINST a verified absorption zone. Large volume + delta spike with NO price progress (Effort vs No Result) = passive institutional defense. Observable via M1 Big Trades: if >= 150 contracts hit at a level and price does not break through, the wall is real. Trade WITH the absorption direction, not against it.

In trending markets, never chase price at session highs/lows. Wait for pullback to HVN ledge or VA boundary. Verify absorption or delta confirmation at the ledge before entering. Stop structural behind the ledge.

For trend-continuation on pullback: entry bar must show clear rejection. SHORT entry: bar must print top_wick_ratio >= 0.35 OR bar_delta < 0. LONG entry: bar must print bottom_wick_ratio >= 0.35 OR bar_delta > 0. If candle closes strongly in the pullback direction without wick rejection or delta flip, skip the trade.

dynamic_rules.topic: Failed Auction Reversal from Big Trades
dynamic_rules.description: When price tests a key extreme (IB Low/High, VAL/VAH) with a Big Trade >= 100 contracts but fails to hold the breakout (Effort vs No Result) and closes back inside with wick_ratio >= 0.40, this confirms trapped traders. Enter contrarian Failed Auction (Long at IBL/VAL traps; Short at IBH/VAH traps). Stop behind the failed wick extreme.

In confirmed strong trending markets, AVWAP anchored to RTH open or session extreme acts as institutional support/resistance. Wait for pullback to AVWAP + Second Drive rejection with delta and volume confirmation. Place stop 20-30 ticks structurally behind AVWAP.

Never enter Failed Auction / Spring / Trap reversal on First Drive (liquidity sweep probe). Wait for pullback and Second Drive retest with volume exhaustion, delta divergence, or active delta flip. Enter only on Second Drive confirmation.

When placing stops, ensure they are positioned beyond significant institutional absorption walls observed in the M1 footprint. For SHORT: stop goes above the nearest BUY cluster with significant volume. For LONG: stop goes below the nearest SELL cluster with significant volume. Add a buffer of 1-2pts to avoid liquidity sweeps.

In strong trending markets, avoid taking partial profits too early. Let the trade run to the full target unless there is a clear reversal signal or delta exhaustion. This prevents leaving money on the table during strong momentum moves.

Avoid trades with R-ratio > 5 unless there is clear institutional absorption or delta confirmation at the entry point. High R-ratio trades often have wider stops and are more susceptible to stop runs.

Avoid continuation trades with R-ratio > 3 unless there is clear institutional absorption or delta confirmation at the entry point. High R-ratio continuation trades in strong trends are more susceptible to stop runs due to wider stops.

session_learnings: All trades were profitable, indicating strong trend continuation and effective use of institutional absorption walls for stop placement.
The strategy successfully avoided high R-ratio trades, with all trades having R-ratios below 3, which contributed to the positive performance.

The probation rule AMT_NEW_02 (Trade Management in Strong Trends) was not tested today as all trades hit their full targets, suggesting the need for more varied market conditions to evaluate its effectiveness.
